column1: # THE ci-runner LANE POLICY (the owner, 2026-11-19: "could any of these decision things could've been handled
# automatically? fix structurally" -- Stage NixOS closures #102 asked him "where should a movies-stage lane rank" and
# Record scrape fixtures #198 "which lane order-independence rows take": both answered by the rules below).
# Where a job's runner lane ranks is decided HERE, not by asking the owner. runner_scheduler.py serves each runner
# class's lanes highest first (MEASURE_LANES, CHECK_LANES); scripts/ci/lane_policy_test.py holds its order to this file.
# A fixer or agent placing a job consults this file and acts; it asks the owner only when no rule here answers, and
# then proposes the row to add (agentctl: `decide[policy-no-rule]: ...; rule: scripts/ci/lane-policy.tsv: <row>`).
# THE RULES, highest first (the `class` column):
#   gate-red-fix          a gate red's fix: before everything (nothing stops a gate fix)
#   landing-check         any other landing check's rows
#   deploy-feeding        work that feeds a deploy or a gate (the staging closures)
#   optional-measurement  identity measurements and other optional runs
#   consumer              a producer's consumer: JUST BELOW its producer's lane (`producer`), never above it
#   exploration           the nightly explorers: last, and none starts while a landing check waits
# NO PRIORITY INVERSION: a consumer never ranks in a lane that cannot start while its producer's priority class runs --
# so a consumer's lane yields to landing checks (`yields_to_landing`) only where its producer's does too.
# runner  rank  lane  class  producer  yields_to_landing  decided
